narrative.overview:
Every machine carries a data plate that says what it is. The family site is the workshop's catalog of such plates: one riveted sheet of brushed steel per engine, read before anything else. The direction is named "Typenschild", German for that plate. A page is light and warm, with deliberately dark passages in smoked oak, the bench the plates lie on, and it closes on one band of dark, oxidized rust. Lettering is a condensed data-plate face; reading text is the system face. Each member is one rendered object of forged steel with a single glowing or rust-orange element, and the greys of the page are warm because those objects are.

The system is dense where a plate would be dense (names, labels, measured facts) and quiet everywhere else. Material gives the pull; restraint and plain language give the trust. It refuses the SaaS hero-plus-feature-cards arrangement and the dark developer-tool default.
keyCharacteristics: Three materials, one job each: brushed steel, dark oak, rust. Everything else is flat, the dark chrome included.
Two ramps hold every color: warm iron greys and oxidized rust.
One prop: the riveted plate, with its measured facts on a tag hanging below it.
One authored scheme on landing pages; no theme toggle there.
Sharp corners; only rivets and chain links are round.
What a thing is comes first; where it comes from comes second.
Two tiers: engines in the family look, applications on light cards under their own logos.

rules.name: The Three Materials Rule
rules.body: Brushed steel is the plate: what a thing is, and the action. Dark oak is the bench: the first viewport and a page's dark bands. Rust is the closing band, once per page. Everything else is flat: the header, the footer, flyouts, code panels and inlays are dark iron without a texture. A new material, or a second prop beside the plate, needs a decision record.

rules.name: The Say-What-It-Is-First Rule
rules.body: A plate carries the name, the plain "what", what it does, and the action. Lineage and measured facts come second: on the hanging tag under a hero, or last and quiet in a catalog row. This is a rule for structure, not only for copy.

rules.name: The One Scheme Rule
rules.body: A landing page is `.fam-page`, which pins the authored light roles whatever the visitor's theme. It has no theme toggle. Documentation follows the system scheme (or the host's explicit `.light` / `.dark`), and keeps Ardo's layout and shapes; the family adds its colors and its chrome, nothing more.

rules.name: The Two Tiers Rule
rules.body: Engines wear the family look. Applications appear in one band, each on a light card under its own logo, with its brand color only in the rule above the card and in its action; the family carries them, it does not dress them.

rules.name: The Independent Members Rule
rules.body: No chain, no pipeline diagram, no entry point. Where two members fit together, the row says so in one sentence. The family site states results qualitatively and never repeats a figure; figures belong to each project's own page.

rules.name: The Shared Pattern Rule
rules.body: A pattern two members' sites need lives in the package, not in each site's stylesheet, and it has a specimen in the kit. Before writing a section by hand, look for it in "Patterns the sites share" in [packages/family/README.md](packages/family/README.md).

rules.name: The Two Ramps Rule
rules.body: Every color is a step of `iron` or `rust`, reached through a role. No cool grey, no third hue, no literal color in a component. (The only literals the build keeps are white and black, for highlights and shadows.)

rules.name: The Oxidized Rule
rules.body: Rust is dark and oxidized, never a saturated orange field. On the rust band the type is plain and light; no display-lettering tricks on rust.

rules.name: The Solid Ink Rule
rules.body: Text on steel is `steel-ink`, solid. `rust-on-steel` is for display lettering only.

rules.name: The One Color Rule
rules.body: Rust is the only hue the family owns. A second accent does not exist; the saturated orange of the rendered icons belongs to the objects, not to the interface.

rules.name: The Foreign Logo Rule
rules.body: A logo that is not the family's (an application's, Sebastian Software's, Sebastian Consulting's) stands on a light ground in its own colors: never on steel, oak, rust or the dark chrome, and never recolored.

rules.name: The Inlay Rule
rules.body: Small type never sits on brushed steel or on rust: a texture's streaks cut into it. On or under a plate it goes on the dark inlay or on the hanging tag: fact labels, the install command, an outlined stamp, what a figure was measured on. As built, nothing below 1.0625rem sits directly on either material. Oak is the ground that carries light text: it is smoked almost to black, so a band's heading, its intro, and a note or stamp legend at 0.9375rem stand on it in the `iron-*` text roles. Measured on the shipped texture, full ink holds about 14:1 at its mean and soft text about 6.7:1, falling to about 4.8:1 on the lightest grain. Nothing smaller or softer than that goes on oak.

rules.name: The Plate Lettering Rule
rules.body: Display type is uppercase and is for what a plate would carry. Two things keep their own case: the "what" line, and an identifier (a file name, a command). An application's name is set in the body face, because it is not the family's brand.

rules.name: The Light-After-Hero Rule
rules.body: Do not pair an oak band directly under the hero when a light section can go there. The kit parts two dark passages with an `iron-line` hairline, which makes the pairing possible, not preferable.

rules.name: The Load Order Rule
rules.body: `tokens.css`, `fonts.css`, `theme.css` (then the optional `docs.css`), `landing.css`, the site's own stylesheet, `chrome.css` last. The site adjusts the kit on equal specificity; the chrome wins its ties. Every landing class is prefixed `fam-`; bare elements are styled only inside `.fam-page` and through `:where()`, so a host rule always wins. The chrome's unprefixed class names (`site-header`, `bar`, `wrap`, `lockup`, `flyout`, `icon`, and the rest listed in the header of `chrome.css`) are part of the package contract. See the Gotchas in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: There is one moving reflection for all plates on a page, mounted once by the hero. No second ambient animation.

rules.name: The Material-Only Depth Rule
rules.body: A shadow means steel. A flat surface never takes one to look like a card; an application's card is parted from the oak by its ground and its top rule.

rules.name: The Round-in-the-World Rule
rules.body: Only what is round in the world is round: rivets (50%) and the links of the tag's chain (0.3125rem on a 0.625rem link). The family draws no other curve; a foreign logo keeps whatever shape it was drawn in.

rules.name: The Honest Comparison Rule
rules.body: A comparison shows the rows where the project is behind, and marks them. A mark that needs qualifying gets its words. Every measurement has its provenance under it. Figures stay on the member's own site; the kit's specimens use invented contenders and invented figures.

rules.name: The 24 Pixel Rule
rules.body: A member's icon is never shown below 24px.

dos: **Do** open a page with one plate on oak: name, the plain "what", what it does, the action; hang the measured facts below it on the tag.
**Do** keep the three materials to their jobs: brushed steel for plates, dark oak for the first viewport and dark bands, rust for the closing band, once. Keep the chrome flat.
**Do** take every color from a role, and every role from a step of the two ramps.
**Do** put small type on an inlay or on the tag whenever it would otherwise sit on brushed steel or on rust, and set text on steel in solid `steel-ink`.
**Do** build landing pages inside `.fam-page`, in the one authored scheme, with stylesheets in the documented load order and classes in the `fam-` namespace.
**Do** follow a hero with a light section.
**Do** show engines in the family look and applications on light cards under their own logos, with the brand color only in the top rule and the action.
**Do** put a small member icon on a steel tile when the ground is dark.
**Do** state what is proven in words on the family site, and leave figures to each project's own page.
**Do** say how two members fit together in one sentence in the row, or as chips under "Runs on", "Pairs with" and "Carries" on a member's page.
**Do** put a pattern two members' sites need into the package, with a specimen in the kit.
**Do** keep the rows where the project is behind in a comparison, and put a `Measured` under every measurement.
**Do** honor reduced motion: the light stands still and the tag does not sway.
donts: **Don't** add a material or a second prop without a decision record.
**Don't** use a plate for something that names nothing; it is not a generic card.
**Don't** set small type on brushed steel or on rust, and don't use `rust-on-steel` below display size.
**Don't** make rust a saturated orange field, repeat the rust band on a page, or set display-lettering tricks on rust.
**Don't** introduce a cool grey, a third hue, or a literal color outside the two ramps.
**Don't** put a texture on the header, the footer, a flyout, a code panel or an inlay.
**Don't** round a corner. Only rivets and chain links are round.
**Don't** put a foreign logo on steel, oak, rust or the dark chrome, and don't recolor it.
**Don't** put a theme toggle on a landing page, or restyle documentation beyond the family's colors and chrome.
